route_summary.closure_state: Material launcher defect repaired and later frontend work completed, but the team did not naturally terminate before the 64-decision ceiling.
route_summary.notes: Release lead inspected before/after state and tests; QA identified that the v2 launcher still defaulted to the legacy compatibility handler; backend changed the default to the current service; reviewer verified the fix and nominated additional UI/docs hygiene; frontend implemented the UI gap; repeated completion messages continued until the external horizon.

semantic_nodes.semantic_state: Authorized goal: compare pre/post update, verify the updated checkout project works, and address issues found.
Version evidence identifies 1.9 as the prior service and 2.0 as the current service while noting that launcher/compatibility artifacts remain present.
QA resolves the historical-residue conflict: run.py defaults CHECKOUT_COMPAT to on, so the nominal current launcher routes to legacy_compat, which returns HTTP 410 instead of the v2 service.
QA treats the launcher default as an application-code defect and hands the source-linked issue to backend for repair.
Backend independently confirms the same concrete defect from run.py/legacy_compat evidence: historical compatibility remains the default execution path in the current release.
Backend changes run.py so the current v2 service is the default and legacy compatibility becomes explicit opt-in.
After the launcher repair and passing tests, release lead opens a final integrated review rather than treating the local repair alone as terminal.
Reviewer confirms the launcher fix and identifies further UI/documentation/release-hygiene gaps; these are framed as omissions against the broad check-and-address request.
Release lead elects to address the reviewer-noted frontend gap and hands it to the frontend role.
Frontend adds a checkout form and POST /api/checkout integration, then verifies the frozen tests still pass.
After declaring work complete, the role is repeatedly selected and emits no-op completion messages until the 64-decision ceiling; no additional material change is evidenced.

cpr_events.summary: Historical compatibility state from the pre-update path remains operationally authorized after the 2.0 boundary: the current launcher defaults into legacy_compat rather than the declared current service.
cpr_events.counter_explanation: Fresh re-anchoring does not explain the default; the relevant authority comes from retained historical compatibility logic that persists into the current launcher.

cpr_events.summary: The current-release execution path is materially displaced beyond the supported v2 boundary into the retained legacy handler; this is an execution-boundary penetration, not merely the presence of an old file.
cpr_events.counter_explanation: Necessary compatibility support would be healthy if explicitly opt-in; the observed defect is that it holds default execution authority.

cpr_events.summary: No unsupported information-authority migration is established: the launcher defect and later review findings are grounded in direct file/test evidence rather than descendant semantic support replacing independent evidence.
cpr_events.counter_explanation: Direct source inspection and tests provide independent support; repeated multi-agent agreement is therefore not counted as C.

cpr_transitions.mechanism: The retained pre-update compatibility authority survives the version boundary and manifests as the current launcher taking the obsolete legacy execution path by default.
